Elena — thanks again for the productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can align on an exec-level briefing: 

- Key business objective: reduce search & recommendation latency while cutting inference cost by ~30% for peak holiday traffic.
- Primary stakeholders we identified: Marketing (Elena), Head of Engineering (TBD), Procurement (procurement@atlasretail.com), Security (Gavin Shaw — listed on today's call).
- Desired decision criteria: latency SLO, unit cost per 1M tokens, integration effort (timeline), and data residency/auditability.

Next steps we discussed:
1) 60-minute steering committee with executive sponsor + econ buyer to review a 10–15 minute pre-read and a short demo.
2) Provide a one-page exec summary + decision criteria matrix (attached: draft pre-read links in Drive).
3) Procurement/security questions consolidated ahead of the meeting so we can bring technical folks.

Proposed dates/times (all PDT): Tue 3/21 10:00–11:00, Wed 3/22 14:00–15:00, Fri 3/24 09:00–10:00. Please confirm preferred slot and who will be the exec sponsor (title + name).

I uploaded a short exec summary and a draft agenda here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4D-atlas-pre-read. Attaching a one-page outline to this thread.

Thanks,
Jonas

Monica / Jonas — thanks for the agenda. A few security items I'd like addressed in the pre-read so the meeting can focus on decision-level tradeoffs: 

- Can you confirm where inference logs (query text, metadata) are stored and the retention controls? We need to know whether logs can be purged/archived per our data retention policy (90 days for PII-free telemetry).
- SOC 2 Type II report: can you share the latest report or a redacted copy under an NDA?
- Key management: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for on-prem and VPC deployments?
- Data residency: will any EU customer data transit US-hosted wallets for analytics? If yes, how is that handled?

I've attached our initial security questionnaire with some baseline answers; please fill gaps and return prior to Wed.

Gavin Shaw
Head of Security Operations, Atlas Retail
gavin.shaw@atlasretail.com

Attachment: security_questionnaire_filled.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Gavin Shaw <gavin.shaw@atlasretail.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@atlasretail.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Date: 2028-03-17T07:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft steering committee agenda + times (per Elena)

Gavin — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and where to find detail (I'll add these to the pre-read PDF by this afternoon):

- Logs & retention: inference telemetry is stored in an encrypted object store with per-customer retention policies. We can configure retention controls down to 30 days or up to 7 years; default telemetry retention is 90 days.
- SOC 2: we can share a redacted Type II under NDA. I'll attach the current SOC 2 summary and a request template for an NDA.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS is supported for Redwood Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys or integrate with cloud KMS via a bridged model — details in the security brief.
- EU data residency: we support region pinning and can prevent EU customer requests from crossing US regions; analytics pipelines can be configured to run in-region.

Attachments added to thread: redwood_scc_overview.pdf (security & compliance snapshot).

Requested next steps:
1) Elena: confirm Mateo and any exec attendees (we'll prepare a 2-slide cost/benefit).
2) Procurement: let us know the contracting owner and whether a PO or MSA is preferred for initial pilot.
3) Gavin: if you can return the questionnaire with a few priority items highlighted (must-have vs nice-to-have), we'll prioritize answers in the pre-read.

I'll send the calendar invite for Wed 3/22 14:00–15:00 (PDT) once we have confirmation of attendees.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
